title: irCLIP
scope: Zarnegar 2016 irCLIP implementation. Extract the single irCLIP route shared by the card image and the poster’s middle row, ending in a physical cDNA library. The standalone IR800–biotin adapter is a reagent/legend with an evidenced ligation interface, not a separate workflow. Neighboring eCLIP/PAR-CLIP rows and chemical drawings, and catalogue mentions of iCLIP/HITS-CLIP, are outside this assigned target. Broad depicted action blocks are retained; primary evidence resolves nuclease-choice and post-RT affinity-purification captions and explains adapter functions and reported library improvements.

operations.label: UV-C crosslink, lyse and fragment
operations.description: Crosslink cellular RNA–protein contacts with the depicted 254 nm UV-C, then prepare a lysate for immunoprecipitation. The source groups crosslinking, lysis and fragmentation; primary methods identify sonication during lysate preparation.
operations.mechanism: UV-C captures RNA–protein contacts; lysis and sonication prepare the material for antibody capture. The later on-bead RNase block performs the distinguishing nuclease trimming.
operations.information_effect: The linked RNA is evidence of captured contacts. This is selective capture chemistry, not a complete census of every cellular RNA–protein interaction.

operations.label: Trim RNA on bead-bound complexes
operations.description: Digest exposed RNA flanking captured RNA–protein contacts while retaining the complexes on beads. The depicted RNase A/RNase I block is interpreted as the paper’s separately evaluated nuclease choices, not a required combined cocktail.
operations.mechanism: RNase acts on accessible RNA around the captured contact. Primary results compare on-bead RNase A and RNase 1 digestions; on-bead RNase A gave the largest recovery of the evaluated optimal RNA fragments.
operations.information_effect: The paper reports improved recovery of RNA fragments suitable for cDNA libraries. RT termination can make cDNA inserts shorter than the recovered RNA, so trimming is not equivalent to defining the eventual insert endpoint.

method_scopes.rationale: The card is headed irCLIP and the candidate collection page is explicitly headed irCLIP: UV-C Crosslinking and Immunoprecipitation with caption A schematic overview of irCLIP. The poster repeats this same route in the middle irCLIP row. The matched Zarnegar paper introduces irCLIP and specifies on-bead trimming, the infrared/biotin adapter, membrane RNA recovery, TGIRT-III, streptavidin hybrid capture, cDNA release, circularization and PCR. These define the scoped implementation. RNase A and RNase I are retained as choices in one depicted digestion block; unshown S1 comparisons do not expand the route. The far-left labeled title icon is descriptive and adds no separate operation. The paper reports improved fragment recovery, cDNA yield and bead-based library recovery; these findings do not imply elimination of RT stops or complete recovery of all interactions.

evidence.quote: 0.2 μL of TIGRT-III reverse transcriptase (Ingex, #TGIRT50) was added to the annealed RNA
cDNA-RNA hybrids were captured by addition of 5 μL of MyOne Streptavidin C1 Dynabeads
Beads were resuspended in 10 μL of cDNA elution/RNA degradation buffer
cDNA was circularized in a thermocycler for 1.5 h at 60 °C.
cDNA-RNA hybrids were captured by addition of 5 μL of MyOne Streptavidin C1 Dynabeads
evidence.rationale: The depicted/primary 3′-biotinylated RNA-linked adapter provides the streptavidin-binding partner. Capture therefore retains the RNA–cDNA hybrid through the template-associated adapter, rather than through an antibody or a biotin copied into cDNA.

corrections.diagram_observation: Both images show one RNase A and RNase I digestion block on immunoprecipitated complexes, with nuclease icons at the flanking RNA. The catalogue describes digestion using RNase A and RNase I.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper compares separate on-bead RNase A, RNase 1 and S1 nuclease treatments and reports on-bead RNase A as the best-performing tested nuclease. Its methods refer separately to RNAse-A- and RNAse-1-digested complexes. The depicted RNase A/RNase I block is retained as one local on-bead trimming block with a nuclease choice; the graph does not assert a simultaneous RNase A plus RNase I cocktail or add the unshown S1 comparison as a target route.

evidence.locator: Captured complex followed by RNase icons; caption RNase A and RNase I digestion
irCLIP row: RNase A and RNase I digestion, with RNA shortened on capture support

evidence.quote: To determine whether a particular nuclease was better at generating optimal RNA fragments, we compared on-bead nuclease digestions across the same panel of RBPs using RNase A, RNase 1, and S1 nuclease.
on-bead RNase A digestions produced the maximal number of optimal RNA fragments
RNAse-A- and RNAse-1-digested complexes were then dephosphorylated with T4 PNK
